request: Analyze GSE302532 for PMID 41078024 (Moderate Chronic Treadmill Exercise Slows Dopaminergic Neuron Loss in a Rat Model of Parkinson's Disease and Alters RNA Content of Circulating Plasma Exosomes.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: total RNA-seq (Takara SMARTer Pico v3) of plasma exosome RNA, NovaSeq X Plus (S2.13.p1, S2.14.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: Cohort 2 only (non-PD, age-matched rats): exercise treatment then exosome molecular biology (S2.1.p1, ABS.p1); n = 4 per group (S2.5.p1); S4.4.p1 states 5 per group (discrepancy). Cohort 1 (PFF histology) has no sequencing.

group: Exercise (1 month treadmill, 20 m/min, 30 min, 5 d/wk)

final.primary_estimand: Difference in plasma exosomal RNA abundance, exercised vs sedentary non-PD rats, blood drawn within 30 min of last exercise (S2.4.p1, S3.4.p1)
planned_contrasts: Exercise vs Sedentary (S2.5.p1, S3.4.p1; paper: 27 RNAs upregulated, Table 2; no downregulated list reported)
final.normalization: CLC Genomics Workbench v25 TPM (GEO data_processing); paper does not describe the DE normalization
final.paper_method: not_reported (GEO data_processing names CLC Genomics Workbench v25.0; the DE test is not named in the paper)

paper_threshold.note: No rule stated. Table 2 lists only upregulated RNAs with raw P-values 3.76E-04 to 0.05 and FC 3.09 to 142.31 (S3.4.p1: 'fold change ranging from 3 to 142'); implied rule raw P <= 0.05 and FC >= 3, up only.

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Two-cohort study; only cohort 2 (exercise vs sedentary, non-PD) was sequenced (S2.1.p1, S2.5.p1). The RNA-seq result is Table 2 (S3.4.p1). The paper states no DE method or threshold; GEO names CLC Genomics Workbench.

checks: GEO: Rattus norvegicus plasma, Sprague Dawley, 4 Sedentary + 4 Exercised, matches S2.5.p1 n=4
TPM file ExerciseExosomeTPMs matches the exosome RNA-seq
Table 2 named RNAs (Npy, Rgs4, Np4, LOC120093427, ...) present as matrix rows

ownership.reasoning: S10.p1 names the accession; sample counts and organism match the methods.

final.note: matrix columns renamed to library names by prep_rename_columns.py (regex ' - (\d+P)_S\d+ (GE) - TPM'); matrix group label prefix (Sedentary/Exercise) agrees with GEO treatment for every library

alignment.reasoning: Deposited TPM columns embed the GEO library name (437P etc.); the prep script renames them exactly and the metadata key is derived from description 'Library name: 437P'. Exact match, no positional alignment.

final.source: GEO data_processing: 'Excel file with TPM values for each sample', CLC Genomics Workbench v25; column headers end in '- TPM'; every column sums to 1e6
final.paper_input: not_reported (paper presents fold change and P-values only)

matrix.reasoning: Column sums are exactly 1,000,000 and headers say TPM; non-integer values. No raw counts are deposited, so count models cannot run.

design.reasoning: Randomized two-arm design, one sample per rat (S2.5.p1). Only male rats (S2.1.p1).

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, no batch, sex, or pairing recorded in GEO or paper; no covariates added.

paper_route.method: CLC Genomics Workbench differential expression (not named in paper; GEO data_processing)
paper_route.reason: CLC's DE test works on read counts; only TPM is deposited and the paper does not name the test

deviations: limma on log2(TPM+1) replaces the unnamed CLC test; zero-variance features dropped by the executor

method.reasoning: TPM supports limma after log2(x+1) under the matrix policy; count methods are not valid on TPM.

paper_threshold.note: implied by Table 2: raw P <= 0.05 and FC >= 3, up only

audit_threshold.label: Table 2 implied rule (raw P <= 0.05, |FC| >= 3); paper reports up only

threshold.reasoning: The paper states no significance rule; workflow default BH < 0.05 applied. The rule implied by Table 2 is reported as a labelled audit for comparison with the 27 upregulated RNAs.

caveats: Paper's DE method (CLC) cannot be rerun from TPM; limma on log2(TPM+1) is a declared deviation.
Paper reports only upregulated RNAs; compare audit up count with 27.
Sample size: GEO and S2.5.p1 give 4 per group, S4.4.p1 says 5 per group.
Exosome libraries are dominated by a few small RNAs (max TPM ~5.7e5), so TPM compositional effects are strong.

study.reasoning: Route is a declared deviation (method). Paper count 27 is upregulated-only.

discrepancies.paper: S2.5.p1 n = 4 per group; S4.4.p1 '5 male rats in each of the exosomal RNA sequencing groups'
not reported; Table 2 shows raw P and FC >= 3
